summary: Ohio State hosts Kent State with Daniels and Grady unlikely to play, according to Day’s Wednesday assessment. Watch the offensive-line combinations, the younger pass rushers and whether the offense can keep drives moving.

items.headline: Day says Daniels and Grady are unlikely to face Kent State
items.tldr: Watch the offensive-line combinations and the rotation at defensive end. Wednesday’s assessment was an expectation, so check the final availability report before treating either absence as certain.

items.headline: Day wants more opportunities for Wilder and Pettijohn
items.tldr: Watch whether fresh defensive personnel can hurry the throw while keeping the quarterback contained. More snaps matter only if they help finish the possession.

items.headline: Timmons forced and recovered a fumble on the opening snap
items.tldr: Watch his tackling and ball awareness continue through a full possession. The early takeaway is useful evidence of what he can contribute.

items.headline: Hawkins made three field goals, then missed from 45 yards
items.tldr: Watch the full kicking operation when a drive stalls. Points from those possessions can decide whether a late defensive stop is enough.

items.headline: Kent State’s DeShields ran for two touchdowns against Wofford
items.tldr: The quarterback is another player the run defense must account for. Watch the edge and open-field tackling when he leaves the pocket.

lead.headline: Make the replacements count.
lead.body: Watch the blocking combinations and the defenders getting an opportunity to pressure the quarterback. Clean assignments should show up before the game reaches the fourth quarter.

matchup.question: What would show progress against Kent State?
matchup.answer: Convert manageable third downs, find receivers beyond the first read, and pressure the quarterback without opening a running lane.

signals.title: Passing balance
signals.detail: Watch Sayin move on when Smith is covered. An available short throw can keep the drive alive.
signals.prompt: How can Ohio State involve more receivers?

signals.title: Third downs
signals.detail: Watch the blocking and route timing after halftime. A stalled series sends the defense straight back out.
signals.prompt: What should Ohio State fix on third down?

signals.title: Defensive front
signals.detail: Watch Wilder and Pettijohn when they get opportunities. Closing the pocket should not leave an easy escape lane.
signals.prompt: What should I watch from Ohio State’s younger pass rushers?

signals.title: Quarterback runs
signals.detail: Watch the defender outside the tackle when DeShields keeps the ball. Make him turn back toward help.
